title: Minimum Time to Revert Word to Initial State II
summary: Given a 0-indexed string word and an integer k, at each second, you must remove the first k characters from word and then add any k characters to the end of word.
statement: Given a 0-indexed string word and an integer k, at each second, you must remove the first k characters from word and then add any k characters to the end of word. Determine the minimum time greater than zero required for word to revert to its initial state.
constraints: word is a nonempty lowercase string with length up to one million and 1≤k≤length.
Each second removes k leading characters and appends any k characters.
Return the minimum positive restoration time using linear-time prefix matching.
hints: A Z value gives the prefix-match length beginning at every possible removed offset.
Build the Z array once, then inspect only positive multiples of k.
Return removed/k at the first offset with Z[removed]≥n-removed; otherwise return ceil(n/k).
That inequality exactly states that every still-forced suffix character equals its original prefix position, while arbitrary appended characters fill the rest.
editorial: That inequality exactly states that every still-forced suffix character equals its original prefix position, while arbitrary appended characters fill the rest.

tests.explanation: At two seconds, the forced suffix a matches the equally long original prefix; appended characters can restore the remainder.
After one removal, suffix aba equals prefix aba, so one second is sufficient.
